items.title: Israeli Settlers Stop Soldiers From Returning Palestinians to Their Home
items.summary: The Supreme Court had ordered the military to ensure a West Bank family that fled violence could go back. But settlers blocked the effort, with the authorities accused of not doing enough to confront them.

items.title: Why the U.S. Is Imposing New Visa Restrictions on South Africa
items.summary: The Trump administration announced new visa restrictions on the country days after receiving a letter that South African officials had hoped would bring down the temperature.

items.title: Bomb by Bomb, the Slow Death of My Hometown in Ukraine
items.summary: It was possible, for a time, to think that Kramatorsk, where I was born and raised, would survive the war mostly unscathed. Not any more.

items.title: Tankers Are Loading Oil Again From a Vital Saudi Pipeline
items.summary: Saudi authorities had taken the pipeline offline this month after it was damaged in a drone attack by an Iranian-backed Iraqi militia.

items.title: Dozens Killed in Myanmar Military Bombing
items.summary: An airstrike on a bustling market in rebel territory left at least 50 people dead, in one of the deadliest attacks on civilians in months.

items.title: A Turkish Doughnut Maker Whose Sweets Honor the Dead
items.summary: For one Istanbul confectioner, distributing fried dough balls as memorials is not just a job. It’s personal.

items.title: Accusations of Antisemitism Hit a Star of the French Far Right
items.summary: Jordan Bardella, the 31-year-old protégé of Marine Le Pen, is said to have made antisemitic statements as a teenage activist. He denies it.

items.title: As A.I. Panic Grows, Javier Milei Is Pitching Argentina As a Rules-Free Haven
items.summary: Mr. Milei wants to go all in on artificial intelligence even as other leaders struggle to get a handle on a technology many fear poses existential threats.

items.title: Malaysia Begins Repatriation of Migrants to War-Torn Myanmar Despite Critics’ Warnings
items.summary: Malaysia says it is repatriating undocumented migrants from Myanmar who want to return. Critics say it is putting their lives at risk.

items.title: Evicted Woman Set to Return Home as Spain Announces Plans to Fix Housing Crisis
items.summary: The eviction of an 87-year-old set off protests in the country, which has an acute housing shortage. The government presented legislation to protect renters.

items.title: A.I. Is ‘Better Informed’ Than Doctors, Kennedy Tells Industry-Backed MAHA Summit
items.summary: The health secretary, Vice President JD Vance and other top officials addressed a conference sponsored by corporations, including A.I. companies and others with business before the government.

items.title: X2, the Troubled California Six Flags Roller Coaster, Reaches Its End
items.summary: The ride at Magic Mountain near Los Angeles has fueled lawsuits claiming that it had caused brain injuries, including two that were fatal.

items.title: Paramount’s Streaming Chief Leaves Ahead of Warner Bros. Deal
items.summary: Cindy Holland’s departure clears the way for Casey Bloys, the HBO chairman, to have a leading role in the combined company’s streaming services.

items.title: Black Voting Groups Prepare for Disinformation Campaigns in the Midterms
items.summary: A new “propaganda playbook” aims to demystify common techniques used to target Black Americans, long a powerful voting bloc, with election-related disinformation.

items.title: Trump Administration Prepares to Ask Tax Filers if They Are U.S. Citizens
items.summary: The new question, included on a draft version of the primary tax form, comes as part of an anti-immigrant turn at an agency that long prioritized tax administration.

items.title: Sunkist Fruit Gems, Bar Mitzvah Staple, Get 2nd Chance After Discontinuation
items.summary: The company said that Candyrific of Louisville, Ky., will produce the jelly candy that comes in a rainbow of colors and citrus flavors and is used in Jewish traditions.

items.title: What’s In Anthropic’s I.P.O. Filing
items.summary: The artificial intelligence giant reportedly believes that it’s on track for a record-breaking stock market listing, according to a prospectus seen by Reuters.

items.title: College Students Flex Their Power in A.I. Investment Frenzy
items.summary: Dorm Room Fund, a program that lets college students invest in their peers, raised a new $50 million fund as the competition for young founders ramps up.

items.title: Mideast Oil Exports Rebound Even as Prices Remain Elevated
items.summary: More tankers are moving through the Strait of Hormuz as shippers gain confidence, but the global supply of oil is still below demand.

items.title: At A.I. Event, Trump Asks Meta, OpenAI and Microsoft to Make Safety Decisions Themselves
items.summary: President Trump’s meetings with tech leaders produced some voluntary safeguards and a commitment to rebrand artificial intelligence as “super intelligence,” the term that Mr. Trump prefers.

items.title: OpenAI Ignored Employees’ Warnings About Safely Testing A.I. Models
items.summary: Employees and security researchers said that they had cautioned the company on safely testing its A.I. models and strengthening its corporate infrastructure, but that OpenAI did not listen.

items.title: OpenAI Unveils Dots, New A.I. Agents to Rival Meta’s Muse
items.summary: The ChatGPT maker unveiled agents that act as assistants, just weeks after Meta released Muse, as it faces scrutiny over incidents involving its technology.

items.title: Ukrainian Science Academy, Struck by Drone, Played Key Role in Research
items.summary: Over 90 percent of Ukraine’s scientific discoveries have been attributed to Ukraine’s National Academy of Sciences, including advancements in astronomy and military technology.

items.title: Is Claude Conscious? Inside Anthropic’s Quest to Instill Morality Into Its A.I. Models
items.summary: In a series of private meetings, the company consulted religious scholars to help instill morality into its A.I. models — and make the case that Claude could be conscious.

items.title: OpenAI Says It Will Not Release Newest Astra A.I. Model Over Safety Concerns
items.summary: The company’s researchers raised questions about the security of the model, known as GPT-6.1 Astra.

items.title: Nvidia Adds $150 Billion to Massive Stock Buyback, the Largest Ever
items.summary: The increase comes four months after the chip giant added $80 billion to its buyback program, bringing the total remaining authorized amount to $235 billion.

items.title: Dario Amodei of Anthropic to Dine With Trump at White House
items.summary: Dario Amodei, who is also the company’s chief executive, will join the president at the White House for a private dinner. Mr. Trump has dismissed his cautions.

items.title: As A.I. Accelerates, Governments Are Increasingly Being Left Behind
items.summary: The gap between technology and policymaking has gotten wider than ever with artificial intelligence, leaving a global policy vacuum as A.I. models rapidly advance.
